project.title: Building a native Dynamic Island for the Mac
project.deck: DynamicIsland is a native macOS app, written in Swift 6 with SwiftUI hosted in AppKit, that turns the MacBook notch into a live, interactive surface: media, timers, files, AI-agent activity, notifications and twenty standalone widgets, all inside one window that never resizes. This site records how it was built, from the first commit on 2 July 2026 to today, and separates what was merged from what has been verified.
project.why: Recent MacBooks have a camera notch but macOS gives it no interactive role. The project asks how far a third-party app can turn that dead area into a useful, glanceable surface using only public, privacy-respecting platform capabilities, and what engineering it takes to make a floating overlay feel native: correct geometry on every display, interruptible motion, keyboard focus that never steals typing, and permissions that are asked for only when needed.
facts: macOS 14.6 or later, menu-bar accessory app
Swift 6, built with Swift Package Manager only
SwiftUI hosted in one AppKit panel
Three signed command-line relays for agent hooks

phases.title: Foundations
phases.summary: Notch geometry, expansion animation, media controls, clipboard history.
phases.objective: Prove that a third-party overlay can sit exactly around the hardware notch and expand without looking like a separate window.
accomplishments: First native app and overlay around the notch
Compact island geometry aligned to the top bezel
First expansion animations and a stable overlay animation strategy
Media controls and early Spotify integration
Clipboard history engine and interface
problems: Compact shoulders and left/right activity regions were unbalanced
Artwork changes flashed against the transition timing
decisions: Derive notch geometry from the screen's safe areas, never from a hard-coded size
Notchless and external displays get a floating island, never a fake notch
phases.lessons: Geometry has to come from the platform's own measurements; every hand-tuned size broke on another display.
phases.verification: Development history only; no recorded hardware acceptance from this phase.

phases.title: Reliability & agent monitoring
phases.summary: Engineering audit; authenticated loopback-only agent bridge (HMAC); agents interface.
phases.objective: Stabilise the foundation, then let the island show what AI coding agents (Codex, Claude Code) are doing, safely.
accomplishments: Foundational reliability audit and correctness repairs
Loopback-only agent bridge with HMAC-authenticated requests
Relay helpers that fail open so they never block an agent
First agent activity views, then an interface overhaul
problems: Agent hooks run outside the app and must never stall the agent
Displayed commands could contain secrets or full paths
decisions: Only one dedicated, authenticated route may ever return an approval decision
Any timeout or transport failure returns no decision, so the agent keeps its own prompt
phases.lessons: Fail-safe defaults matter more than features when an overlay can influence another program.
phases.verification: Automated tests for authentication, ingestion and privacy projection.
phases.limitations: Claude Code and generic producers are observation-only by design.

phases.title: Interaction model
phases.summary: Two-finger gestures, camera hand navigation, native audio, voice recording, per-app volume.
phases.objective: Make the island feel like part of macOS: trackpad gestures, keyboard behaviour and native audio and camera integration.
accomplishments: Two-finger gesture navigation and native Settings organisation
Camera hand navigation with separate gesture and pointer modes
Native widgets, audio surfaces and notch context menu
Voice recording with optional transcription
Per-app volume mixing using Core Audio process taps
problems: Gesture-only layouts drifted off the notch centre
Tab continuity broke when a page attached late
Post-merge CI failures needed repair without weakening native assertions
decisions: One physical swipe equals exactly one media command
Experimental surfaces (Lock Screen widgets) stay opt-in and isolated
phases.lessons: Gesture handling needs explicit ownership of each input session, or momentum tails trigger a second action.
phases.verification: Automated tests plus a stabilisation checkpoint with review fixes.
phases.limitations: Lock Screen widgets rely on private system interfaces and remain experimental.

phases.title: Native widget re-architecture
phases.summary: One widget registry, Shortcuts tab, 20 standalone widgets, Teleprompter, accessibility validation.
phases.objective: Replace a compound productivity page with independently addressable native widgets that share one registry and one layout system.
accomplishments: One native widget registry and a Shortcuts tab with a trackpad-scrollable icon row
Standalone widgets: Notes, Stay Awake, Window Snap, Voice, Reminders, Background Removal, Camera, Lyrics, Screen Recording, AirDrop, File Conversion, Calendar, App Volume and more
Quick Terminal, synced lyrics and a lid-fold experiment (Mac Duo)
Teleprompter with live speech
Clean-room study of a reference app's motion and notifications
problems: Several pull requests touched the same shared files in parallel
Widget sizes depended on their siblings
decisions: Widget size is a semantic grid class (Compact 1x1, Standard 2x1, Large 2x2), never a scale factor
Only an integration owner edits shared navigation and overlay files
phases.lessons: A single source of geometry truth removed a whole class of layout bugs at once.
phases.verification: Automated tests, native acceptance captures and a release review with explicit untested items.
phases.limitations: Several widgets still need checks on a real Mac (see Roadmap).

phases.title: Polish & performance
phases.summary: Notification banner, MCP connections, permission prompts, Agents composer, motion parity, performance pass.
phases.objective: Make everyday use calm and fast: notifications, permissions asked at the right moment, motion tuned against a reference, and measured performance work.
accomplishments: Notification banner with history, reply and opt-in support for other apps
MCP connection status and permission prompt handling
Calm new-chat composer with model and reasoning controls
Animation speeds and delays matched to a reference app, with Faster and Slower presets
Performance pass guided by Time Profiler captures and a frame-pacing probe
problems: Collapse animation built the hidden page needlessly
Pollers re-published equal values and re-rendered every observer
Three stacked pull requests were merged into each other instead of into main
decisions: No full-history work inside per-frame view code
phases.lessons: Measure first: the profiler, not intuition, found the hot paths.
phases.verification: 3,159 automated tests passing locally on 9 Nov 2026; frame-pacing logs from the owner's Mac.
phases.limitations: The full 120 Hz performance gate is still open (#51).

challenges.title: Morphing the island without resizing the window
challenges.problem: Expanding the island by resizing its window caused flicker, and wider pages grew to one side only, measured at 26 pt.
challenges.investigation: Frame-by-frame inspection showed the canvas offset animating separately from the shell during a tab change.
challenges.rootCause: SwiftUI received the new size one update after the panel resized, so the content was centred on a stale proposal.
challenges.solution: One fixed, maximum-size transparent panel. SwiftUI morphs the visible shell inside it, the panel never animates in AppKit, and the canvas is pinned top-leading so it never re-centres on the proposal.
challenges.verification: Shell-morph invariant tests lock the horizontal centre and the top edge through every morph.
challenges.lessons: When two layout systems disagree for one frame, remove one of them from the animation instead of compensating per frame.

challenges.title: Collapsing without leaving content behind
challenges.problem: On collapse, page content sometimes stayed visible while the shell shrank, or the island stayed black after a lost animation.
challenges.investigation: Logging each collapse generation showed SwiftUI animation completions that never arrived.
challenges.rootCause: Collapse relied on animation callbacks that SwiftUI does not guarantee to deliver.
challenges.solution: A fixed order: children exit, the exit is acknowledged, then the shell collapses. Each exit runs on its own clock, and a newer collapse acknowledges immediately. No timers decide the order.
challenges.verification: Unit tests on the exit tracker cover lost completions and repeated collapse requests.
challenges.lessons: Never make correctness depend on an animation finishing.

challenges.title: A drag preview that would not settle
challenges.problem: Dragging a widget below another made the preview jump back and forth, so that drop position was unusable.
challenges.investigation: Recording pointer position against the shell size showed a loop: the preview resized the shell, which moved the target, which changed the preview.
challenges.rootCause: The pointer was resolved against geometry that the preview itself was changing.
challenges.solution: Resolve the pointer against the layout as it was when the drag started, keep editing layouts top-anchored, and let the shell grow but never shrink during a drag.
challenges.verification: Drop-resolver and workspace layout tests; bounce-free springs keep velocity when the target changes.
challenges.lessons: Feedback that changes its own input needs a fixed reference frame.

challenges.title: Typing into an overlay that never takes focus
challenges.problem: Clicking a text field in the island did nothing: keystrokes still went to the app behind it.
challenges.investigation: The island is a non-activating panel so that ordinary clicks never steal focus from the user's work.
challenges.rootCause: A non-activating panel does not become the key window, so its text fields never receive key events.
challenges.solution: Only when a click makes a real text input first responder does the panel claim key status, one run-loop turn later. Automatic focus, such as the terminal appearing, never holds the island open.
challenges.verification: Focus-policy tests plus a native keyboard acceptance harness.
challenges.lessons: Widen focus rules only for the exact control that needs it; a broad rule would steal typing on every click.

challenges.title: Agent approvals that fail safe
challenges.problem: Letting the island approve an agent's command is useful but dangerous: a bug or outage must never approve anything.
challenges.investigation: Threat review of every path from an agent hook to a decision: replay, wrong session, expiry and transport failure.
challenges.rootCause: A generic event channel cannot tell a real approval request from a forged or stale one.
challenges.solution: One dedicated, HMAC-authenticated route with exact session and request matching, expiry and one-shot replay protection. Timeouts, shutdown and transport errors return no decision, so the agent keeps its own prompt. Displayed command text is sanitised and bounded.
challenges.lessons: In a safety feature, 'no answer' must be the default answer.

challenges.title: Replying to Messages without guessing the chat
challenges.problem: A reply typed in the island must reach exactly the conversation it came from, and the app must not store message content.
challenges.investigation: Notification titles and display names are ambiguous: two chats can share a name.
challenges.rootCause: Matching by display name can send a message to the wrong person.
challenges.solution: Resolve each notification to one chat through provider-native identifiers in a read-only database; unresolved or ambiguous notifications get no reply option. Send through Apple Events with typed parameters, no script text, and report success only once the message appears in that exact chat.
challenges.verification: Resolver and send-result tests; message bodies are never logged or persisted.
challenges.lessons: When identity is uncertain, offer less, not a guess.

challenges.title: A long agent transcript that froze the app
challenges.problem: With a very long transcript visible, the whole app stuttered.
challenges.investigation: Time Profiler showed the main thread re-processing the same huge text over and over.
challenges.rootCause: SwiftUI asked the text view to update repeatedly with unchanged text, and each update re-scanned all of it.
challenges.solution: Cache the applied text and skip identical updates, while still processing changes to active state, Reduce Motion and animation timing.
challenges.verification: Streaming-text state tests cover the unchanged-text path.
challenges.lessons: View update calls are not change notifications; compare before doing work.

challenges.title: A permission that disappeared on every rebuild
challenges.problem: After each development rebuild, Screen Recording stopped working and the Allow button did nothing.
challenges.investigation: macOS records the permission against the app's code signature; ad-hoc builds get a new signature hash every time.
challenges.rootCause: The old grant no longer matched the new build, and the system silently refused to prompt again.
challenges.solution: Remember per build that a request was made and show remove-and-re-add guidance instead of looping; use a stable local signing identity so grants survive rebuilds.
challenges.verification: Gated live tests for the recorder pipeline; the guidance path is merged.
challenges.lessons: Some failures belong to the platform's security model; the honest fix is to explain them clearly.

challenges.title: Showing other apps' notifications honestly
challenges.problem: The first design promised a marker for every notification on the Mac, but public APIs only expose an app's own notifications.
challenges.investigation: Documentation review and a clean-room study of how a reference app behaves; tracked in issue #50.
challenges.rootCause: Reading other apps' notifications needs explicit user consent and access the system does not grant by default.
challenges.solution: A notification banner with history and reply. Other apps' notifications are shown only after the user opts in and grants Full Disk Access, and are held in memory only.
challenges.verification: Merged in #77; issue #50 closed as superseded by the banner design on 9 Nov 2026.
challenges.lessons: Scope features to what the platform legitimately allows, and say so in the interface.

challenges.title: Who is allowed to turn the camera on
challenges.problem: The camera could start when a view merely appeared, and stopping it from one place did not always release it.
challenges.investigation: Several features share one capture session: the mirror widget, hand navigation and Settings preview.
challenges.rootCause: Appearing on screen was treated as consent to capture.
challenges.solution: Capture starts only from an explicit Start; collapsing the island stops mirror-owned capture; hand navigation keeps its own ownership.
challenges.verification: Capture-ownership tests. Open in #47: the stop button is visible only on hover, and stopping a session owned by hand navigation has no confirmed path yet.
challenges.lessons: Privacy-sensitive resources need an explicit owner, not a reference count.

challenges.title: Measuring smoothness instead of assuming it
challenges.problem: Expanding, collapsing and switching tabs sometimes felt slower than a reference app on a 120 Hz display.
challenges.investigation: An opt-in frame-pacing probe logs p50/p95/p99 frame times per transition; Time Profiler captures on the owner's Mac located main-thread bursts.
challenges.rootCause: Work during animation frames: building a hidden page during collapse, history-wide work in per-frame code, and pollers re-publishing equal values.
challenges.solution: No page build during the shell shrink, cached derived data, changed-only publishing, and decorations paced to the display refresh rate.
challenges.verification: Merged in #81 with automated tests. The full gate in #51 (10-minute soak, GPU, 60 Hz external display, Low Power Mode) has not been run.
challenges.lessons: A frame budget is 8.3 ms at 120 Hz; only measurement shows what spends it.

challenges.title: Three merged pull requests that never reached main
challenges.problem: Pull requests #79, #80 and #81 were reported merged, but their code was missing from main.
challenges.investigation: Comparing merge commits with main showed each one merged into the branch of the pull request below it in the stack.
challenges.rootCause: The bottom pull request (#78) was squash-merged first, and the stacked ones were then merged into their old base branches instead of main.
challenges.solution: A single landing pull request (#83) merges the stack tip into main. Its tree was verified to equal the tested tip plus one unrelated change.
challenges.verification: Tree comparison against the tested tip; awaiting the owner's merge.
challenges.lessons: With stacked pull requests, retarget each to main before merging, or merge bottom-up with merge commits.

items.name: Notch-aware island shell
items.detail: One stable panel; the shell morphs between collapsed and expanded around the physical notch, or floats on notchless displays. Expanded, it hosts several widgets side by side.

items.name: Live Activities
items.detail: An internal activity model (not Apple's iOS-only ActivityKit); the collapsed island shows one winner chosen by deterministic priority, with its own width around the notch.

items.name: Workspace editor
items.detail: Drag to reorder and resize widgets in semantic sizes (Compact, Standard, Large) and add them from the dock; Apply commits once, Cancel restores.

items.name: Gestures
items.detail: Two-finger navigation; one swipe equals one media command.

items.name: Media
items.detail: Now Playing with capability-driven controls (Spotify Web API, Music, system sources) and an output picker.

items.name: Synced lyrics
items.detail: Line-synced lyrics in the Media widget and a companion view.

items.name: App Volume
items.detail: Per-app volume through Core Audio process taps (visible in the expanded island and workspace editor captures). Off by default; asks for System Audio Recording only when turned on. Experimental label removed on 9 Nov 2026 after the owner's hardware check (#84).

items.name: Voice recording
items.detail: Native recorder with optional transcription.

items.name: Shortcuts tab
items.detail: A trackpad-scrollable row of native app icons. Apps such as Finder and Safari launch externally; island tools open as a standalone widget in place.

items.name: Focus timer
items.detail: A scrubbable time ruler with Focus and Break presets, zoom and one completion sound; the idle minimum is one second on every input path.

items.name: Stay Awake
items.detail: Prevents idle sleep for a chosen time, with a visible countdown.

items.name: Clipboard history
items.detail: Opt-in history of copied text and images with pinning, tags and excluded apps; nothing is recorded until it is turned on.

items.name: AirDrop, File Shelf and file conversion
items.detail: Drop files to share them, keep them on a shelf, or convert images and audio.

items.name: Quick Terminal
items.detail: A small shell in the island that runs one command at a time and kills only its own process group.

items.name: Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Window Snap
items.detail: Standalone widgets in Compact, Standard and Large sizes.

items.name: Teleprompter
items.detail: Script reading with live speech tracking; Reduce Motion reads phrase by phrase.

items.name: Notifications
items.detail: Banner, history and reply; other apps only on explicit opt-in. Previews hide during protected interactions (see the workspace editor capture).

items.name: Messages replies
items.detail: Replies to the exact chat through Apple Events; no Accessibility scripting.

items.name: Agents composer
items.detail: Start a chat with Codex or Claude, with model and reasoning controls and both providers' 5-hour and weekly usage (#80, landing on main through #83).

items.name: Agent monitoring
items.detail: Codex and Claude Code sessions through a loopback-only, HMAC-authenticated bridge, with a live feed of session events.

items.name: Approvals
items.detail: Codex permission requests can be approved from the island; failure always returns no decision.

items.name: Native Settings window
items.detail: Grouped panes for every module, previews with sample content, and permission setup.

items.name: Lock Screen widgets
items.detail: Opt-in and off by default; relies on private system interfaces.

items.name: Mac Duo lid fold
items.detail: A display-fold effect when the lid closes; the physical fold has not been verified on hardware (#47).

parts: Notch geometry from screen safe areas

decisions.title: One stable window, with the shape morphing inside it
decisions.decision: Keep one maximum-size transparent panel fixed and let SwiftUI morph the visible shell inside it.
alternatives: Resize the window for each state
Swap between separate collapsed and expanded windows
Compensate the window position every frame
decisions.consequences: No flicker or one-sided growth; click-through must be shape-aware so the empty panel area never blocks the desktop.

decisions.title: Swift Package Manager only, no Xcode project
decisions.context: Builds are run by scripts, agents and CI.
decisions.decision: Build, test and package with SwiftPM and a packaging script that owns Info.plist and signing.
decisions.consequences: Reproducible command-line builds; every privacy usage string and helper binary is declared in one script.

decisions.title: An internal Live Activity model
decisions.context: Apple's ActivityKit and Dynamic Island APIs are for iPhone, not the Mac.
decisions.decision: Model activities internally and choose one winner by deterministic priority for the collapsed island.
decisions.consequences: Predictable presentation; each activity has its own width profile around the notch.

decisions.title: Approvals fail safe; most producers only observe
decisions.context: Agents can ask permission to run commands.
decisions.decision: Only one authenticated Codex route may return a decision; everything else is observation-only, and failures return no decision.
decisions.consequences: Less convenience, no path for an outage to approve anything.

decisions.title: Widget size is a semantic class, never a scale factor
decisions.context: Widgets looked different depending on their neighbours.
decisions.decision: Compact, Standard and Large are grid spans from one unit; each size has its own layout, and the saved size owns the geometry.
alternatives: Scale widgets to fill the shell
decisions.consequences: A widget looks the same everywhere; narrow hosts wrap instead of shrinking.

decisions.title: Public, consented platform access only
decisions.context: Several features touch notifications, messages, camera and screen.
decisions.decision: Use public APIs, ask for each permission at the moment a feature needs it, and keep anything relying on private interfaces opt-in and labelled.
alternatives: Scrape other apps' interfaces through Accessibility
decisions.consequences: Some features are narrower than competitors', and the interface says why.

decisions.title: Match motion to a measured reference
decisions.context: Transitions felt slower than a reference app.
decisions.decision: Study the reference app's behaviour clean-room and adopt its timings as defaults, with Faster and Slower presets around them.
decisions.consequences: Comparable feel with an original implementation; timings are named tokens rather than scattered numbers.

decisions.title: A local-first thesis record
decisions.context: The app repository is private and hosted CI minutes are exhausted.
decisions.decision: A scheduled job on the author's Mac publishes aggregate counts and content-free placeholders to this public site; narratives are written by hand.
decisions.consequences: No private material leaves the private repository; new work appears as 'review pending' until it is written up.

pipeline: Strict signature checks on the app and its three helpers

evidence.title: Automated tests
evidence.detail: 3,159 tests, 0 failures, 87 skipped, in a local run on 9 Nov 2026. Skipped tests are gated live-hardware checks (camera, audio, screen recording).

evidence.title: Native acceptance harnesses
evidence.detail: Built-in modes render every widget size, Settings pane and live activity with sample content and save captures; the screenshots on this site come from them.

evidence.title: Hosted CI
evidence.detail: GitHub Actions minutes are constrained, so recent runs are local. Results here are local unless a pull request says otherwise.

evidence.title: Accessibility
evidence.detail: Reduce Motion paths for every animated surface, accessibility labels and actions on controls, keyboard focus policy. No formal VoiceOver audit has been recorded.

evidence.title: Performance
evidence.detail: Frame-pacing probe and profiler-guided fixes merged; the full 120 Hz gate is open (#51).

evidence.title: Hardware acceptance
evidence.detail: Installed-app checks on a real Mac are tracked on the Roadmap; merges are not presented as hardware verification.

supervisorQuestions: Is automated testing plus a recorded hardware checklist an acceptable evaluation method, given that some checks need physical hardware?
Should the thesis treat the AI-agent integration as a core chapter or as one case study among the widgets?
Is a clean-room behavioural study of a reference app acceptable as part of the research method?
